title: Constructibility and intervals under normalized finite reduction
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a noetherian scheme T [pqf-def-locnoeth], and an arbitrary complex K of detailed completed integral coefficient modules. For any n>=0 and integers a,b, its derived reduction modulo varpi^(n+1) [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] is intrinsic finite-torsion constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and has nonzero cohomological support contained in [a,b] if and only if the n-th constant derived reduction of integralDetailedTransport(K) [def-sfb-integral-completed-coefficient-transport] is IsGE a and IsLE b and has constructible cohomology over the finite quotient coefficient ring [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. No order condition on a,b or completeness condition on K is needed.

source.place: Section 6.5, convention before Definition 6.5.1; Lemma 4.2.12 and Lemma 6.8.2(1). Coefficient-presentation supplement to Proposition 6.8.11(3).

proof.text: Apply the normalized completed coefficient comparison and its derived restriction square to the quotient projection. The uniqueness of a left adjoint identifies the detailed derived scalar extension with the quotient extension. Compose with the constants-to-continuous-functions comparison to obtain an isomorphism from the transported constant reduction to restriction of the detailed reduction.
Exact coefficient restriction commutes with each homology functor. As an equivalence it preserves and reflects zero objects. Thus vanishing below a and above b is equivalent on both reductions.

Restriction along a coefficient ring isomorphism preserves finite constant module models on every stratum; use inverse restriction to reflect them. Its scalar action agrees with the fixed-coefficient encoding by naturality of sheafification. The two constructibility encodings identify the resulting predicates.

Combine the cohomology comparison and the vanishing characterization of IsGE and IsLE. In the reverse direction the support is a subset of the finite integer interval, so its finiteness clause follows as well. This also handles empty intervals and the zero complex.

proof_origin.place: Explicit comparison of the two normalized coefficient presentations in the detailed-category clause of Proposition 6.8.11(3); the proof is implemented completely in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem integralDetailedFiniteReduction
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T] (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (K : DerivedCategory (WeilConjectures.scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E T))
    (n : ℕ) (a b : ℤ) :
    (intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E (n + 1)
        (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)) T
        ((WeilConjectures.scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E T n).obj K) ∧
      proEtaleCohomologicalSupport
        ((WeilConjectures.scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E T n).obj K) ⊆
          Set.Icc a b) ↔
    (((pbcConstantReduction T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).obj
        ((integralDetailedTransport T l E).obj K)).IsGE a ∧
      ((pbcConstantReduction T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).obj
        ((integralDetailedTransport T l E).obj K)).IsLE b ∧
      DerivedCategory.homologyProperty
        (@IsConstructibleProEtaleCoefficientModuleSheaf T
          (PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n) _
          ((pbcIntegralDatum l E).quotientFinite n))
        ((pbcConstantReduction T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).obj
          ((integralDetailedTransport T l E).obj K)))
